summary: Build practical climate budget tagging, green PFM, and fiscal risk skills. Develop usable tools and a reform roadmap. Enquire today.
lede: Climate-responsive public financial management and budget tagging training helps officials connect climate priorities with resource ceilings, programme structures, procurement, cash releases, and year-end reporting. You will learn to apply Climate Budget Tagging, the PEFA Climate Framework, the OECD Green Budgeting Framework, and IMF Climate-PIMA concepts to strengthen the link between policy and public spending. Practise building tagging logic, testing expenditure data, measuring budget execution, identifying climate-related fiscal risks, and creating a management dashboard. The course also introduces green PFM reform sequencing, climate finance disclosure, and scenario analysis, with practical templates and an implementation roadmap for ministry or subnational government use.
audienceIntro: Green PFM requires collaboration across budget, treasury, planning, climate, audit, and reform functions. This course suits experienced public finance professionals who need to convert climate priorities into traceable allocations, controlled expenditure, and decision-ready fiscal evidence.
modules: Green PFM Foundations and Policy Links
prerequisites: You should have practical experience in public budgeting, treasury operations, public expenditure analysis, fiscal policy, public investment, audit, or climate finance programming. Prior exposure to a budget classification system, medium-term expenditure framework, or financial management information system will help. No programming is required. Advanced climate fiscal risk and digital analytics concepts are taught at operational application level, while AI-assisted classification receives controlled conceptual and workflow-level treatment.
